message: what is ORS and how do i make it at home if there is no pharmacy
response:
ORS (oral rehydration solution) replaces the water and salts lost through diarrhoea or vomiting. Ready-made ORS sachets are best, and they are free at health facilities. If you have none, you can make it at home (WHO recipe):

- 1 litre of clean water (boiled and cooled)
- 6 level teaspoons of sugar
- half a level teaspoon of salt

Stir until dissolved. Too much salt is dangerous, so measure carefully. Give small sips often, keep breastfeeding babies, and make a fresh batch every day. Go to a health facility quickly if the person cannot drink, is very sleepy, has blood in the stool, or is not getting better.
key_points: oral rehydration solution replaces water and salts; 1 litre clean (boiled, cooled) water + 6 level teaspoons sugar + half level teaspoon salt; give small sips often

message: what is sickle cell disease
response: Sickle cell disease is a genetic disorder characterized by the presence of abnormal hemoglobin molecules called hemoglobin S (HbS). These abnormal hemoglobin molecules cause red blood cells to become rigid, sticky, and shaped like crescents or sickles under certain conditions. This leads to various symptoms and complications, including chronic anemia, vaso-occlusive crises, organ damage, and increased susceptibility to infections.
key_points: inherited (not contagious) blood disorder; red cells become sickle-shaped; pain crises, anaemia, infections; lifelong care, fluids, follow-up
